problem_summary.summary: Return the number of characters in the final word, where words are maximal runs of non-space characters.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a string containing English letters and spaces with at least one word. Return the last word's length.
constraints: s contains English letters and spaces
At least one word is present

brute_force.explanation: Trim the ends, split on one or more spaces, then return the length of the final token. This is concise but constructs an array and tokens.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Trimming removes outside spaces and splitting on runs of spaces produces the words in order, so the last token is exactly the final word.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — trimming and splitting scan the input.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) for the trimmed string and token array.

optimized.explanation: Scan backward over trailing spaces, then continue backward over the final non-space run. The distance between the two boundaries is its length.
optimized.correctness_idea: The first loop skips only trailing spaces; after it stops, the next contiguous non-space run is precisely the last word. Counting that run gives its exact length.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) worst case; the scan touches at most each character once.

steps.condition: The characters at indices 14 and 13 are spaces.
steps.action: Decrement index until it points to 'w' at index 12.

steps.condition: The character is not a space.
steps.action: Count backward across review, ending at index 6 with length 6.

edge_cases.handling: The backward scan skips them before counting the word.
The scan counts the full non-space portion.
The scan stops at the first separator before the final word and ignores earlier content.
